To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the age associated decline in CD28 expression correlates with an increased susceptibility of T cells to CD95 mediated cell death.
the ageing T cell population is more susceptible to CD95 mediated apoptotic death due to a decrease in expression levels of activation markers CD28 and CD25.
T cells become less susceptible to apoptosis via CD28 and CD25 co-stimulation with age, and that this correlates with decreased CD28 and CD95 expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of ageing on the expression of CD28 in human T cells, and the impact on CD95 mediated apoptosis.
the effects of age on the expression of T cell activation receptors and the susceptibility of T cells to apoptosis.
the role of CD95/CD28/CD25 expression in T cell activation and apoptosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T cell activation is a complex process that involves multiple signals.
CD4+ T cells undergo a greater number of PD than CD8+ T cells.
T cell activation and susceptibility to apoptosis is age associated and that the decreased expression of CD25 is a key biomarker of T cell ageing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the decrease in T cell activation markers, CD25 and CD 28, with age, correlates with increased susceptibility to CD 95 induced apoptosis in T cells.
the ageing of T cells is associated with a decline in expression of CD25, and CD28, and that these changes correlate with increased susceptibility to CD 95 mediated apoptosis.
the ageing T cells are less susceptible to apoptosis via the CD95/CD28/CD95-L pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD4 and CD28 are the most important biomarkers in the ageing T cells, which can be used to predict susceptibility to apoptosis.
CD25 and CD95 expression is upregulated with activation of T cells, but is lost in an age dependent manner.
the decreased expression of CD25 with increasing PD is a major biomarker of ageing in T cells and may be used to determine the age of a T cell culture.
